blocks.md: This lesson follows **Authority Transitions** in *Supervisory Intervention* (Vol IV).

blocks.source: Vol IV, Supervisory Intervention, § Authority Transitions
blocks.md: When a remote assistant takes manual control of the arm after the mobile base has slowed or stopped for a blocked aisle, authority must move between proposers on a single permission tick without two of them ever commanding the same channel, and it must not outlive a proposer that falls silent. The transfer names each actuator channel and assigns it to a single owner; linear blending of two competing proposers is no substitute for choosing who is in charge.

questions.q: The section **Authority Transitions** develops one of the chapter's claims. Which one?
options: Autonomous chunks and manual sessions hold separate leases on the safety MCU's clock, so a silent policy, a dropped link, or an incapacitated operator loses authority to a state-matched local fallback.

The authority record binds a sealed static authority manifest to a per-tick evidence tuple of time, authority state, measured state, proposed and admitted commands, so every handover is reconstructable and attributable.
Blending human and policy commands works only when goals are unimodal and every intermediate blend is admissible; across modes a convex combination is a new, unchecked command.
A remote assistant is admitted only if reaction budget, handshake latency, manual lease, and blend window fit the remaining clearance, and remote assistance is never a safety layer.
